explanation: Because its ribs became its shell, a turtle's shoulder blades ended up inside its ribcage, an arrangement found in no other living animal with a backbone.

claims.text: A turtle's upper shell is formed largely from its broadened ribs, fused with its backbone and bony plates.
A turtle's shell is not formed from its hip bones, shoulder blades or skull bones.
Turtles are the only living vertebrates whose shoulder blades lie inside the ribcage.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: three listed; high: c3 (superlative); standard: c1 and c2. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology (it holds countries, languages, currencies, cities, elements, Nobel Prizes, Olympic Games, World Cups, art collections and Natural Earth), so none applies, and the high-risk claims need web evidence from checker A; one search on turtle shoulder blades inside the ribcage should cover c1 and c3. rivalTest: Collarbones and breastbone were kept out of the options because bones derived from them help form the lower shell, which would make a second defensible answer. The stem says 'much of its shell' because the backbone and dermal plates join the ribs in the upper shell. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: turtles and tortoises live on every continent apart from Antarctica. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 26 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a multiple-choice item. doubts: none. c3 holds 'only', which the tooling's riskReason enum lacks, so it is marked superlative.
